svg.title: VLA-Mender Framework with Detailed Multi-Agent Repair Workflow
svg.desc: Publication-style framework diagram emphasizing task-parallel repair agents, the persistent failure-mode state machine, GPU-local evaluation runtime, artifact ledger, and campaign-local experience library.
svg.text: VLA-Mender: Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Repair and Learning Framework
Each task is repaired by one dedicated agent; each failure mode is governed by a persistent state machine and one current experience slot.
PRE-REPAIR: REPRODUCIBLE FAILURE DISCOVERY AND VERIFIED HANDOFF
shared reset, action, gripper, success semantics
normalized tasks + complete FM seed-job inventory
Repair Stage — Task-Parallel Agents, Persistent Failure-Mode State Machines, and Experience-Guided Candidate Search
repairs one assigned task and launches peer agents
one task only; cross-task access forbidden
one fixed worker pool + service group per GPU
waits when agent slots are unavailable; tasks are never combined
The runtime enforces leases but does not create agents.
2. Per-Task Agent Workflow (repeated independently for every task)
analyze task phases and diagnosed mechanisms; inspect observation API, examples, skills, and relevant campaign experience
Open one persistent state machine per Failure Mode (FM)
all prepared seeds are open from the start; state survives agent/process restarts
promote the expanded initial baseline before later mechanism rounds
iterate while evidence supports further search
dynamic seed dispatch → fixed worker pool → subprocess isolation
one SAM3 / Contact-GraspNet / PyRoKi service group per GPU
Only success adds coverage; only policy_failure enters clusters.
VLA prefix [0, reset) + selected repair suffix
sim hash · splice state · optical flow
updated checkpoint → standardized rollout → next repair campaign
